source: Own measurement (2026-11-28, folder rack-anchor5), ten-rod rack with every place equally likely: the privileged reference (solution/solve.sh; controller RodOracle, bounded Cartesian servo with the torso guard, with the reference token, which gives it ground truth and assisted grasping) on the six fixed hidden shifts of tests/hidden/shifts.json, each through the grading path (solve.sh + verify.py + the kit's wire) in the task's final cell: ten hanging rods, one released per event at a place drawn uniformly, feed on its own timetable, a cell that does not wait for the controller (reply time = the controller's CPU time), physical grasping for contestants, rubber finger pads (friction 2.0). Real simulator on the author's cluster (H200, Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX on the CPU; the card was shared with other simulators during the measurement; the reference's replies cost about 1 ms of CPU each and no late step was charged). Per shift, seed: score (placed/20): 4418: 0.85 (17), 7093: 1.00 (20), 1256: 1.00 (20), 8830: 1.00 (20), 3607: 1.00 (20), 5971: 1.00 (20); mean 0.975. All probes passed on every shift, no bystander moved. Shift 4418 lost three rods in its last third; the cause is not known. An earlier measurement of the same cell before the torso guard (job 62808903) gave 0.80, 1.00, 0.45, 1.00, 1.00, 1.00 (mean 0.875): on shift 1256 the torso sagged after the ninth rod and the arm stayed out of reach; with the guard that shift is 1.00 in two runs. The six seeds are the first six drawn; none was selected or replaced after measuring. full_at 0.90: the reference's own six-shift mean has to stay above 0.8775 to earn the full reward.
note: part_pickup_score = mean per-part credit (1.0 in the tote, 0.5 held for 1 s, 0 lost, -0.5 per disturbed bystander), mean over the hidden shifts.
